checks: Each active plane at a mark has mean L_i under its probability row by affinity and the full barycenter. Since it majorizes L and the row L-mean is also L_i, its nonnegative gap vanishes in the row. Positivity of the row coefficient in the decomposition and bounded positive L imply the row is absolutely continuous with respect to mixed volume.

If two active source planes have unequal continuous slopes, their equality cuts a d-volume-null hyperplane in every sampled fiber, including counting codimension in dimension one. The row has mass one and cannot be carried by their common zero gaps there. This proves agreement of all source continuous slopes, without imposing equality of their base slopes.

A finite union of unequal-slope coincidences and fiber boundaries is mixed-null. On the complement each active plane has the same continuous slope, and the gaps to the other planes give the own-fiber derivative. Contact of each positive row with a source plane identifies its target label almost everywhere.

Multiplying the row decomposition by the label test and by (1,w) gives the first identity using the row mass and barycenter. Multiplication by L gives the second identity because the row L-mean is L_i. Indicators of individual labels show exactly the positive source and target labels, and their count is bounded by the number of occurrences.
